description: Validated CV model weights per modality. Place files under MODEL_WEIGHTS_DIR after clinical validation.

monai-unet.task: organ segmentation (spleen) — NOT lung nodule detection

weights.CT: spleen_ct_segmentation/ (full bundle dir: configs/ + models/model.pt, fetched via monai.bundle.download)

monai-unet.notes: Weights present on disk does NOT enable this backend — see clinical_use_gate_env. MRI intentionally not wired (no standardized single-sequence Model Zoo bundle); a medical director must select one before implementation. Only used as a fallback in engine.py when neither totalsegmentator nor lung_nodule_detection is approved (least informative of the three CT backends). True lung-nodule *detection* is now implemented separately — see lung_nodule_detection below.

totalsegmentator.task: whole-body organ segmentation, 117 classes ('total' task, fast/3mm model)
totalsegmentator.source: TotalSegmentator (Wasserthal et al.) — pip package, self-downloads its own nnU-Net weights on first run
totalsegmentator.weights: auto-download to TOTALSEG_WEIGHTS_PATH/Dataset297_TotalSegmentator_total_3mm_1559subj on first approved use, or pre-fetch via scripts/download_weights.py --warmup-totalsegmentator
totalsegmentator.notes: Weights present on disk does NOT enable this backend — see clinical_use_gate_env. confidence_score is a coverage-based heuristic (organs found vs expected), NOT a per-voxel probability — this model's simple Python API returns hard labels only. Tried before the single-organ MONAI spleen bundle in the routing chain since it covers more organs.

lung_nodule_detection.task: 3D lung nodule detection (discrete candidate boxes + scores), NOT segmentation
lung_nodule_detection.source: MONAI Model Zoo bundle 'lung_nodule_ct_detection' — RetinaNet + ResNet50-3D-FPN, trained on LUNA16
lung_nodule_detection.weights: lung_nodule_ct_detection/ (full bundle dir, fetched via monai.bundle.download)
lung_nodule_detection.notes: Weights present on disk does NOT enable this backend. Runs in engine.py's CT multi-model merge alongside totalsegmentator (organ boundaries + discrete nodule candidates are complementary, both included in the merged result when both are approved). Sliding-window ROI reduced from the bundle's own default (512,512,192) to (96,96,48) for CPU tractability — a tuning choice that itself needs validation, not assumed equivalent to the bundle's documented config. Box coordinates are voxel-space, not yet transformed to patient world coordinates (needs full DICOM affine, only approximated here).

breast_density_classification.task: BI-RADS breast density classification (A-D), NOT lesion/malignancy detection
breast_density_classification.weights: breast_density_classification/ (full bundle dir, fetched via monai.bundle.download)
breast_density_classification.notes: Weights present on disk does NOT enable this backend. Single 2D image classification (not volumetric) — mammography goes through the existing single-instance DICOM fetch path, no series/volume assembly needed. Density category only, explicitly not framed as a cancer-detection output.

mri-unest-brain.task: whole-brain structural segmentation, 133 FreeSurfer-derived structures, single T1-weighted series
mri-unest-brain.source: MONAI Model Zoo bundle 'wholeBrainSeg_Large_UNEST_segmentation' (Vanderbilt University + MONAI team)

weights.MR: wholeBrainSeg_Large_UNEST_segmentation/ (full bundle dir: configs/ + models/model.pt, fetched via monai.bundle.download)

mri-unest-brain.notes: Weights present on disk does NOT enable this backend — see clinical_use_gate_env. The bundle's own metadata.json says outright: 'This is an example, not to be used for diagnostic purposes.' Reports segmented-structure counts and named-structure voxel counts (currently: left/right lateral ventricle) as a technical/anatomical review — NOT framed as detecting any specific pathology (no tumor/hemorrhage/hydrocephalus claim). Input is downsampled to 64x160x160 before inference (native 512x512x~25-200 caused repeated OOM kills on this box's 15GB RAM at the bundle's native resolution across its 133-channel output) — a CPU-tractability approximation needing its own validation before being treated as spatially precise. Single T1-weighted series only: the incoming study's T1 series is picked by a SeriesDescription substring heuristic (fetch_t1_series_instances_dicom in orthanc_client.py), not a validated sequence classifier — an unfamiliar naming convention silently falls back to the largest series in the study, which may not be T1. Verified against 2 real patient studies (ICH Egmore pediatric brain MRI) end-to-end: both completed in under 2 minutes on CPU, correctly identified the T1 series among 8 and 40 total series respectively, segmented 130/133 and 132/133 structures with genuine softmax-derived confidence (0.61, 0.56).

mri-brats-tumor.task: multimodal brain tumor subregion segmentation (tumor core / whole tumor / enhancing tumor) from T1+T1c+T2+FLAIR
mri-brats-tumor.source: MONAI Model Zoo bundle 'brats_mri_segmentation' (SegResNet, trained on the BraTS challenge dataset)

weights.MR: brats_mri_segmentation/ (full bundle dir: configs/ + models/model.pt, fetched via monai.bundle.download)

mri-brats-tumor.notes: Weights present on disk does NOT enable this backend. The bundle's own reported validation performance (Dice ~0.85 WT / 0.86 TC / 0.79 ET) is on properly BraTS-preprocessed data and is NOT a claim about accuracy here — this integration stacks four real but imperfect approximations on top of raw clinical DICOM: (1) MISSING T1c on every real patient tested (no contrast series was acquired) — plain T1 is duplicated in its place, which specifically compromises the enhancing-tumor channel since enhancement is a contrast-uptake signal a non-contrast image cannot show; (2) classical-CV skull-stripping (Otsu threshold + largest connected component + hole-fill), not a validated brain extractor; (3) T2/FLAIR rigidly registered onto the T1 grid via SimpleITK Mattes mutual information — real registration, but rigid-only (no deformable step) and never checked against ground truth for these studies; (4) input downsampled from the bundle's native 240x240x160x4 to 64x128x128x4 for CPU tractability on this box's 15GB RAM. Registration sampling seed fixed to 42 after finding the SAME real patient's SAME data produced different tumor voxel counts (55 vs 0) on two runs purely from unseeded random sampling — now reproducible run-to-run, which is not the same as accurate. Verified end-to-end against 2 real patient studies: one returned a small, low-confidence whole-tumor flag (70 voxels at the downsampled resolution, confidence 0.55, barely above the 0.5 threshold — read as a marginal/borderline signal, not a confident finding), the other returned a clean negative (0 voxels, all three channels). Ground truth is not available for either case, so neither result has been confirmed correct or incorrect.
